header: Node-to-node encryption for Amazon OpenSearch Service
content:
Node-to-node encryption provides an additional layer of security on top of the default features of
Amazon OpenSearch Service.
Each OpenSearch Service domain—regardless of whether the domain uses VPC access—resides
within its own, dedicated VPC. This architecture prevents potential attackers from intercepting
traﬃc between OpenSearch nodes and keeps the cluster secure. By default, however, traﬃc
within the VPC is unencrypted. Node-to-node encryption enables TLS 1.2 encryption for all
communications within the VPC.
If you send data to OpenSearch Service over HTTPS, node-to-node encryption helps ensure that
your data remains encrypted as OpenSearch distributes (and redistributes) it throughout the
cluster. If data arrives unencrypted over HTTP, OpenSearch Service encrypts it after it reaches the
cluster. You can require that all traﬃc to the domain arrive over HTTPS using the console, AWS CLI,
or conﬁguration API.
Node-to-node encryption is required if you enable ﬁne-grained access control.
